overview.text: Betelgeuse, also designated Alpha Orionis, is an orange-red red supergiant marking Orion the Hunter’s shoulder. Its size, brightness, and relative closeness make it one of the few stars whose surface astronomers have resolved and monitored directly. It is a semiregular variable: its brightness rises and falls, with occasional irregular changes. During the Great Dimming of late 2019 and early 2020, it faded dramatically; observations showed that cooled ejected gas formed dust that temporarily obscured it, rather than the dimming signaling an imminent supernova. As a massive, evolved star, Betelgeuse is expected eventually to explode as a supernova, but the event is not predicted soon.

key_facts.text: Betelgeuse marks Orion’s shoulder and is also called Alpha Orionis.
Its brightness varies semiregularly, with both recurring cycles and occasional irregular changes.
In late 2019 and early 2020, a cloud of dust formed from ejected gas temporarily dimmed the star; the event was not evidence of an imminent supernova.
Astronomers have directly imaged Betelgeuse’s surface, making it unusually useful for studying changes in a red supergiant.
Betelgeuse is expected eventually to become a supernova, but that does not mean an explosion is imminent.
